evaluation.positioning_hook: A timid office clerk with reality-bending powers is forced into a monster-hunting squad of misfits and has to save London by eating the one thing that unlocks him.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise has a clean, easy-to-sell engine: an underqualified office worker gets dragged into a supernatural kill team, with a clear comic-action promise and a satisfying underdog payoff. The appeal is strongest for genre audiences who like irreverent ensemble energy and power-reveal escalation.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands quickly in the opening pages: Francis wakes in a ruined space, cuts to a bizarre logistics office, and is then conscripted into a mission because of his anomalous status. The rules are intentionally playful, but the central engine is easy to track.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Francis is a strong lead shape: anxious, self-effacing, secretly powerful, and emotionally legible in the way he resists then rises. The team around him gives the story a lively social field, with Ploy, Clara, Hal, Toast, and Doreen each carrying distinct comic and tactical energy.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script commits to a very specific comic register: bureaucratic death logistics, retro-futurist tech, monster-hunting coworkers, and absurdly specific food jokes like maple miso donuts and the hot dog trigger. The voice is confident and willing to be weird in a way that gives the material identity.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The story moves briskly from office disruption to mission briefing to London confrontation, and the action escalates cleanly once the team meets the zombie target. The structure is straightforward and readable, with the climax built around Francis finally discovering how his power works.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The most memorable idea is the combination of mundane office labor with cosmic anomaly management, where death toll spreadsheets sit beside a squad of bizarre operatives. The hot-dog trigger and the outburst meter give the concept a fresh, immediately playable logic.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: Comirum feels like a lived-in institution with its own rules, slang, hierarchy, and visual identity, from the comic-sans death board to the retro-futurist gear and article-based authority. The world suggests a larger bureaucracy and a broader supernatural ecosystem beyond the immediate mission.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The tone is sharply defined: profane workplace banter collides with monster violence, absurd character design, and deadpan bureaucratic menace. The script knows exactly how silly, gross, and dangerous it wants to feel.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: Beneath the comedy, there are intriguing seeds around Francis being an anomalous being, the threat of erasure, and Doreen’s guarded authority. The script hints at a larger mythology and a more personal cost structure without overexplaining it.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The team dynamic is the engine: Francis and Ploy have immediate chemistry, Clara and Hal create a volatile comic partnership, and Toast’s deadpan friction with everyone adds texture. The group feels like a unit that can generate scenes from almost any pairing.

Toast is a robot character requiring voice/performance capture or prosthetic/CG integration

technical.vfx_details: Glow effects, multicolor power bursts, teleportation/light transport, regeneration, glitch effects, and creature enhancement are all present but not constant.
technical.sfx_needs: Creature prosthetics, practical blood, limb loss, weapon transformations, and impact effects.

rights_flags.detail: Microsoft Excel is referenced as a recognizable software equivalent.
Google is referenced as a search-equivalent platform.
Comic Sans is specifically named in the death board gag.

platform_fit.recommended_lane: streaming or premium-cable genre feature lane
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: festival-to-platform or streamer genre launch, with franchise-adjacent worldbuilding potential.

cost.note: The footprint is mostly contained to offices, streets, and a single creature fight, but the powers, creature work, and action staging push beyond microbudget.

cast.note: The ensemble is manageable in size, though the script depends on distinct, highly specific character types and one creature performance.

location.note: The story is not sprawling, but it does require multiple interiors, London exteriors, rooftop action, and night work.

content.note: Profanity, violence, blood, limb loss, and zombie-style creature combat keep this in mature territory without pushing into extreme content.

rights.note: The script uses a few generic brand references and no major life-rights or IP-dependent material.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The office world is the engine.
strengths.what_it_means: The death-toll logistics division gives the script a fresh institutional frame that makes the supernatural feel bureaucratic, funny, and scalable. That kind of setting is instantly pitchable because it turns monster action into workplace procedure.
strengths.evidence: The comic-sans death board, the spreadsheet work, and Doreen’s office authority all establish Comirum as a functioning machine.

strengths.what_it_means: He’s a timid pencil pusher with reality-breaking power, which gives the lead both comedy and wish-fulfillment. Actors get a role that can play fear, embarrassment, surprise, and eventual release in one package.
strengths.evidence: He panics through the briefing, insists he does nothing, then ultimately fires the multicolor beam that destroys the zombie.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The ensemble has immediate comic chemistry.
strengths.what_it_means: Every team member arrives with a distinct rhythm, which makes the group feel castable and scene-generating. That’s valuable for producers because it creates a built-in social engine, not just a hero plus helpers.
strengths.evidence: Ploy’s bass-heavy swagger, Clara’s coke-fueled chaos, Hal’s bravado, and Toast’s deadpan contempt all collide in the briefing and fight.

strengths.what_it_means: The script commits to profanity, absurdity, and creature violence without losing clarity, which gives it a distinct voice in the genre lane. It feels like a world where a death spreadsheet and a zombie brawl belong in the same breath.
strengths.evidence: The donut jokes, the “pencil pusher” insults, and the British zombie’s grotesque tea-time banter all coexist cleanly.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The power mechanic is simple and playable.
strengths.what_it_means: Francis’s outburst meter and the food-trigger reveal create a clean visual rule that audiences can track immediately. That kind of rule-based escalation is useful for marketing because it gives the climax a satisfying “aha” payoff.
strengths.evidence: The wrist device climbs from 20 to 90, and the hot dog becomes the key that unlocks his final blast.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The creature fight has a strong escalation path.
strengths.what_it_means: The London sequence keeps changing tactics, which gives the action a sense of invention rather than repetition. That makes the set piece feel like a showcase for both the team and the world’s rules.
strengths.evidence: The zombie survives gunfire, loses limbs, climbs walls, and is finally erased by Francis’s beam.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The world suggests a larger mythology.
strengths.what_it_means: Comirum, SINONs, containment breaches, and article-based authority all hint at a bigger system beyond this mission. That gives the material franchise-adjacent value even as a feature, because the audience can sense a wider universe.
strengths.evidence: Doreen’s references to top brass, containment, and Francis being erased imply a broader hierarchy and threat structure.

whats_special.headline: SINON has a sharp, marketable hook: a frightened office clerk in a death-logistics bureaucracy discovers he’s the team’s most dangerous anomaly. The script’s biggest asset is its voice — a profane, retro-futurist monster-comedy with a cast of vivid misfits, a clean power mechanic, and a world that feels big enough to launch beyond one mission.

lead_characters.name: Francis Booker
lead_characters.hook: Francis is a nervous, self-protective office drone who looks like he’d rather disappear than be noticed, until the world forces him to become the most important person in the room. He’s funny because he’s overwhelmed, appealing because he’s decent, and compelling because his body is literally hiding a power he doesn’t understand. The role lives in the gap between meekness and latent force.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of part actors chase when they want to play a full arc from humiliation to release. It offers comic timing, physical panic, and a final power turn that lands like a cathartic reveal, with the same emotional satisfaction as Jesse Eisenberg’s volatility in The Social Network or Daniel Kaluuya’s contained escalation in Get Out.

lead_characters.name: Ploy
lead_characters.hook: Ploy is a loud, fearless, bass-driven operator who treats danger like a social event and speaks with the confidence of someone who’s already survived worse. She’s flirtatious, abrasive, loyal, and funny in a way that makes her feel like the team’s pulse. She also functions as Francis’s first real believer, which gives her warmth under the swagger.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a showcase for a performer who can command a room, flip from teasing to tactical, and make bravado feel like armor. The part has the kind of kinetic, scene-stealing energy that lives in the lane of Michelle Rodriguez in Fast & Furious or Janelle Monáe in Glass Onion.

lead_characters.name: Clara
lead_characters.hook: Clara is a feral, glamorous chaos engine: coked up, flirtatious, violent, and weirdly charming, with a mouth that never stops and instincts that are always half a second ahead of everyone else. She’s the kind of character who can turn a briefing into a party and a firefight into a joke. The role is all volatility, appetite, and comic danger.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: Actors love roles that let them be outrageous without losing control, and Clara is built for exactly that. It’s a juicy, high-voltage part in the tradition of Jennifer Tilly in Bound or Jennifer Coolidge in White Lotus, where the performance can be both hilarious and unpredictable.

lead_characters.name: Hal
lead_characters.hook: Hal is a swaggering bruiser who performs confidence so hard it becomes its own kind of comedy. He’s loud, self-mythologizing, and weirdly likable, with a masochistic streak that makes him feel dangerous and game at the same time. He gives the team muscle, but his real function is attitude.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a great part for a performer who can weaponize physicality and comic bravado. It has the same pleasure zone as Dave Bautista in Guardians of the Galaxy or John Cena in Peacemaker: big presence, surprising timing, and a character who can be both threat and punchline.

lead_characters.name: Toast
lead_characters.hook: Toast is a dry, contemptuous machine with a superiority complex and a deadpan that cuts through the chaos. He speaks like an algorithm that has decided everyone around him is beneath contempt, which makes him a perfect comic foil inside a messy human team. The character’s appeal is in precision, disdain, and timing.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a gift for a performer with a sharp voice and a taste for controlled, ironic delivery. The role sits in the same pleasure space as Alan Tudyk-style performance work or a sardonic animated sidekick that gets to puncture every room it enters.

lead_characters.name: Doreen
lead_characters.hook: Doreen is the hard-edged authority figure who keeps the entire machine moving while making it clear she’s not sentimental about anyone’s survival. She’s stylish, intimidating, and pragmatic, with just enough buried feeling to suggest she knows exactly how brutal the system is. She reads like a boss who has already made peace with impossible decisions.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a strong authority role for an actor who can project command without flattening into stereotype. It has the same gravitas-and-ice energy as Viola Davis in a command role or Frances McDormand when she’s carrying institutional authority with dry wit.

director_appeal.hook: A director who loves worldbuilding through behavior, not exposition.
director_appeal.detail: This material rewards someone who can stage action as character comedy and make a bizarre bureaucracy feel tactile, legible, and cool. The right director gets to balance creature spectacle, ensemble banter, and a very specific visual language of retro-futurist office absurdity.

buyer_appeal.lane: genre-forward streaming feature / premium-cable fantasy-action lane
buyer_appeal.detail: The script is sized for a contained but effects-aware production: a small core cast, limited locations, and one major creature set piece. It fits buyers looking for distinctive, exportable genre material with a strong hook, a clear ensemble, and franchise-adjacent world potential without tentpole spend.

considerations.area: The feature plays as a compact launchpad.
considerations.detail: The current shape reads like a strong first installment or proof-of-concept feature, with a world and team that could support more stories. A future pass could consider how to foreground the emotional spine of Francis and Doreen a touch earlier so the climax lands with even more personal force.

considerations.area: The opening is built for immediate curiosity.
considerations.detail: The cold open and office reveal are doing a lot of heavy lifting in a good way; protecting that speed will help the script keep its momentum. If anything is expanded, it should be the sense of what Francis stands to lose inside Comirum, because that makes the conscription sting even harder.

considerations.area: The ensemble is strongest when it’s in motion.
considerations.detail: The group chemistry pops most clearly once everyone is together in the briefing and on the street, so preserving that combinatorial energy is key. One direction would be to keep giving each pairing a distinct tactical or comic function so the team feels even more indispensable.

considerations.area: The power rule is memorable and marketable.
considerations.detail: The outburst meter and food-trigger logic are the kind of clean, visual mechanics that help a genre feature travel. Clarifying the rule just enough for audience anticipation — without sanding off the weirdness — would make the climax even more satisfying.

considerations.area: The London set piece carries the movie.
considerations.detail: The rooftop-and-alley sequence is the feature’s big showcase, and it already has a strong escalation rhythm. A future pass could sharpen the geography of the chase so the audience feels the team’s coordination even more vividly as Francis comes online.

considerations.area: The script lives in a mature genre lane.
considerations.detail: The profanity, blood, limb loss, and grotesque creature design place this squarely in an adult genre space rather than four-quadrant family territory. That’s an asset for positioning, because it gives the movie a clear audience and a confident tonal identity.
